commodity_commentary: Commodity markets were led by energy, where WTI crude held at US$103.02/bbl, up 0.82% on the week and 64.33% year-over-year, and Brent rose 2.20% to US$110.14/bbl, both reflecting the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption that the World Bank flagged as the biggest energy price surge in four years.13 Natural gas eased 1.31% to US$3.079/MMBtu, holding 8.36% below a year ago. Precious metals diverged from crude: gold slipped 1.64% to US$4,497.00/oz and silver fell 10.41% to US$76.27/oz, though silver remained 136.04% above its year-ago level — the steepest 12-month move in the complex — after a year of safe-haven demand against the energy-led inflation regime12. Base metals firmed, with copper up 14.29% to US$6.32/lb (+36.21% year-over-year) as China halted sulfuric-acid exports from May and Q1 2026 Chinese GDP printed +5.0%18. Agriculture advanced, with wheat up 1.02% to US$671.75/bu — a fresh 52-week high — and the Nutrien potash proxy up 5.31%; lumber added 1.89% to US$593.00/mfbm. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the energy move to 59 oil and gas projects valued at $97.58B and the metals strength to 390 mining projects valued at $227.11B18. Western Canadian Select, uranium, nickel and canola carried no priced series this cycle and are marked unavailable.

commodities.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
commodities.context: Crude Oil (WTI): US$103.02/bbl (+0.82% week-over-week) — crude held above the US$100 mark as the Strait of Hormuz disruption sustained the supply premium the World Bank described as the biggest energy price surge in four years13. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the level to 59 oil and gas projects valued at $97.58B and 613 transport and logistics projects valued at $44.13B exposed to fuel-cost dynamics. WTI is up 22.86% on the month and 64.33% year-over-year against a one-year average of US$70.25/bbl, sitting below its 52-week high of US$112.95/bbl set during the spring supply shock11. If WTI holds above US$100/bbl, the database's 35 NAICS-21 mining and extraction projects carrying $81.39B in tracked value would maintain the netback assumptions cited in public filings, with the broader 59-project oil and gas pipeline retaining measurable exposure to sustained crude levels11.

commodities.name: Western Canadian Select
commodities.context: Western Canadian Select: Data unavailable for this commodity this week. The dossier carries no WCS pricing or WCS/WTI differential this cycle; WCS discount analysis is reported as not available.

commodities.name: Crude Oil (Brent)
commodities.context: Crude Oil (Brent): US$110.14/bbl (+2.20% week-over-week) — the global benchmark outpaced WTI as OPEC output posted its biggest monthly drop in decades and the cartel announced only a symbolic output rise during the Hormuz closure1415. Brent is up 68.05% year-over-year against a one-year average of US$74.44/bbl, holding below its 52-week high of US$118.35/bbl. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the global crude strength to the 59 oil and gas projects valued at $97.58B in the pipeline15.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.context: Natural Gas: US$3.079/MMBtu (-1.31% week-over-week) — the Henry Hub benchmark eased, diverging from crude as the oil-driven supply premium did not extend to gas, leaving the contract 8.36% below its year-ago level against a one-year average of US$3.53/MMBtu13. The price sits well below its 52-week high of US$6.80/MMBtu. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links gas pricing to LNG-linked projects within the 59-project oil and gas pipeline valued at $97.58B, where export economics track the gap between domestic prices and Asian delivered cost11.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.context: Gold: US$4,497.00/oz (-1.64% week-over-week) — bullion eased as higher U.S. Treasury yields following the Fed's April 29 hold raised the opportunity cost of holding the metal, though it retained a 41.33% year-over-year gain against a one-year average of US$4,013.24/oz12. Gold sits below its 52-week high of US$5,318.40/oz. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties precious-metals pricing to 390 mining projects valued at $227.11B; mining and quarrying GDP rose +3.6% year-over-year over the same window8.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.context: Silver: US$76.27/oz (-10.41% week-over-week) — silver posted the sharpest weekly decline in the complex on the same yield-driven pressure that weighed on gold, yet it held 136.04% above its year-ago level, the steepest 12-month gain among tracked commodities, against a one-year average of US$58.60/oz and a 52-week high of US$115.08/oz12.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.context: Copper: US$6.32/lb (+14.29% week-over-week) — copper firmed as China halted sulfuric-acid exports from May, tightening the global supply chain, with Q1 2026 Chinese GDP at +5.0% reinforcing demand and the metal nearing a record US$6.58/lb on May 1218. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links electrification and grid demand to 390 mining projects valued at $227.11B; copper is up 36.21% year-over-year against a one-year average of US$5.17/lb19.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.context: Wheat: $671.75/bu (+1.02% week-over-week) — wheat advanced to a fresh 52-week high of $671.75/bu, up 26.98% year-over-year against a one-year average of $545.06/bu, as the energy-cost backdrop lifted input and transport expenses across Prairie agriculture13.

commodities.context: Canola: Data unavailable for this commodity this week. The timeseries carries only a single level datapoint (CAD$733.20/t) with no computable deltas; referenced qualitatively only.

commodities.name: Potash (Nutrien)
commodities.context: Potash (Nutrien): US$98.45 (+5.31% week-over-week) — the Nutrien equity proxy for potash rose, up 22.74% year-over-year against a one-year average of US$87.79 and below a 52-week high of US$114.41, on resilient global fertilizer demand channels tied to Saskatchewan production19. No spot potash feed is available, so the Nutrien equity is used as the proxy.

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.context: Lumber: US$593.00/mfbm (+1.89% week-over-week) — lumber firmed as Canadian housing starts jumped +17% in April to a 279,317 SAAR, lifting construction-input demand, though the contract remained 1.66% below its year-ago level against a one-year average of US$585.45/mfbm and a 52-week high of US$695.50/mfbm5. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties lumber to 72 NAICS-23 construction projects valued at $9.96B and 211 residential projects valued at $32.23B; construction GDP was -0.5% month-over-month despite the starts rebound5.
